════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT THE FIRST REAL CONTRACT BROKE

Three walls in the first ten minutes, all the same mistake: a schema built
from a specification rather than from a document somebody actually has.

(a) THE SCHEMA COULD NOT SAY "APPROXIMATELY".

    BOPEU's retainer is confirmed at APPROXIMATELY P18,000/month. That is the
    honest state of the fact. org_contracts had nowhere to put it:
    retainer_amount is numeric(12,2), and org_contracts_amount_agrees_with_kind
    REQUIRES it non-null for a retainer. The only way to record the contract at
    all was to write 18000.00 — a number that reads as exact, that the monthly
    handover would bill from, and that nobody would know to question.

    A schema that can only store precise numbers does not make the world
    precise. It makes the imprecision invisible, which is worse than refusing
    the row.

    An approximate amount now MUST carry a note. An unexplained "about" tells
    the next reader the number is soft and nothing about why.

(b) `campaign` WAS NOT A FORMAT. Two of BOPEU's rows are self-directed
    challenges — a walking challenge and a movement challenge. Nobody delivers
    them at a time and a place. 'other' would have lost the only thing that
    makes them different.

(c) `vendor` WAS NOT A PRACTITIONER KIND. Health screening is delivered by an
    external provider. The column admitted only 'advisor' and 'counsellor',
    both Key Wellness staff. Recording vendor work as advisor work inflates
    every capacity and utilisation figure that counts practitioner time —
    quietly, and in the direction that flatters us.

NOT ADDED, ON PURPOSE: `group_session`. The programme spec names it; the schema
already has `group`. Two values for one idea means half the rows use each
within a month. BOPEU's group sessions are recorded as `group`.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE ROLLBACK REFUSES TWICE, AND BOTH ARE EXERCISED

  guard 1 — refuses while any contract is marked approximate. Dropping the
            flag does not make the number exact; it makes it LOOK exact, which
            is the state M4b exists to end.
  guard 2 — refuses while any row uses campaign or vendor. Narrowing the checks
            would orphan a record of a real session, and re-classifying vendor
            work as advisor work would corrupt capacity figures.

The suite creates all three, so it hits both guards every run and clears them
deliberately, reporting "m4b guard 1 ok" and "m4b guard 2 ok".

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BLOCKED, AND WHY

BOPEU's contract row is NOT yet created. Two things are missing and neither is
mine to invent:

  1. THE 19-ROW PROGRAMME. `claude/bopeu-workplan-2026.md` is not in this
     working tree — there is no `claude/` directory here at all — and it is not
     anywhere in the build history. Dates, topics, pillars, formats and
     statuses for a real client cannot be reconstructed from the schema.

  2. THE ACCOUNT MANAGER. "Lone, presumably — confirm" is not a confirmation,
     and CLAUDE_CONTEXT.md's standing rule is that ownership is never guessed:
     configured, or absent-and-flagged.

A FINDING THAT CHANGES WHAT TASK 1.4 CAN SHOW: BOPEU has TWO members and
org_report_data returns insufficient_cohort for every quarter of 2026 — before
any of this. Recording nineteen activities will not change a single reported
figure for BOPEU, because the base-5 cohort floor fires first. The regression
will correctly show no movement, and that is NOT evidence the activities
landed. It also means Lone cannot get a BOPEU report out of this system today
regardless of how complete the programme record is.
